title: Streamline pathology foundation model by cross-magnification distillation

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Streamline pathology foundation model by cross-magnification distillation》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Foundation models (FM) have transformed computational pathology but remain computationally prohibitive for clinical deployment due to their massive parameter counts and high-magnification processing requirements.

evidence.text: Foundation models (FM) have transformed computational pathology but remain computationally prohibitive for clinical deployment due to their massive parameter counts and high-magnification processing requirements.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Streamline pathology foundation model by cross-magnification distillation》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-5】We trained XMAG on 3.49 million images curated from publicly available datasets and evaluated performance across seven clinically relevant histopathology analysis tasks spanning multiple cancer types.

【Abstract · abstract-1-8】We further explore end-to-end XMAG training as a direction for task-specific adaptation of the compact model.

evidence.text: We trained XMAG on 3.49 million images curated from publicly available datasets and evaluated performance across seven clinically relevant histopathology analysis tasks spanning multiple cancer types.
We further explore end-to-end XMAG training as a direction for task-specific adaptation of the compact model.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Streamline pathology foundation model by cross-magnification distillation》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-6】Across four WSI-level classification tasks, XMAG achieved an average AUC within 1% of substantially larger foundation models while delivering up to 29.5-fold faster encoder-level processing, corresponding to an encoder throughput of 8.8 WSIs per minute in a controlled patch-encoding benchmark.

【Abstract · abstract-1-7】We also found that performance differences remained task-dependent, with larger gaps observed for fine-grained tasks such as ISUP grading and patch-level phenotyping.

evidence.text: Across four WSI-level classification tasks, XMAG achieved an average AUC within 1% of substantially larger foundation models while delivering up to 29.5-fold faster encoder-level processing, corresponding to an encoder throughput of 8.8 WSIs per minute in a controlled patch-encoding benchmark.
We also found that performance differences remained task-dependent, with larger gaps observed for fine-grained tasks such as ISUP grading and patch-level phenotyping.
